dimensions.assessment: Affects all digital commodity exchanges, brokers, dealers, associated persons, qualified digital asset custodians, and retail participants nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: To provide for a system of regulation of the offer and sale of digital commodities by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes extensive federal registration, capital requirements, daily trading recordkeeping, segregation of customer assets, and conflict of interest rules.
dimensions.evidence: Each digital commodity broker and digital commodity dealer shall meet such minimum capital requirements as the Commission may prescribe

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes $150,000,000 in appropriations and mandates ongoing fee collection from registered entities to cover administrative costs.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act... $150,000,000

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Commodity Exchange Act extensively, creates new statutory sections, establishes an Office of the Digital Commodity Retail Advocate, and requires numerous joint rulemakings with the SEC.
dimensions.evidence: The Commodity Exchange Act is amended by inserting after section 5h (7 U.S.C. 7b-3) the following: SEC. 5I. REGISTRATION OF DIGITAL COMMODITY EXCHANGES.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent regulatory authority and continuous oversight structures for digital commodity markets.
dimensions.evidence: this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect on the date that is 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act.

card.title: Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act

summary: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act establishes a regulatory framework for digital commodities under the jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). It sets up registration, operational, and reporting requirements for digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers, and creates protections for software developers and customer asset segregation.

affected_groups.effect: Must register with the CFTC, meet minimum capital and financial resource standards, maintain trade records, and follow strict customer protection and asset segregation rules.
affected_groups.group: Digital Commodity Exchanges, Brokers, and Dealers

affected_groups.effect: Protected from being classified as regulated intermediaries under the Act for engaging in basic blockchain activities like compiling network transactions, operating nodes, or providing user interfaces.
Receive enhanced disclosures, asset segregation protections in bankruptcy, and representation through a newly established Office of the Digital Commodity Retail Advocate.
Tasked with writing extensive new rules, registering intermediaries, conducting market surveillance, and establishing fee structures to fund oversight.

key_provisions: Grants the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over spot and cash digital commodity transactions offered or traded on registered entities or by registered intermediaries.
Requires digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers to register with the CFTC and comply with rules regarding trading, recordkeeping, capital, and conflict of interest mitigation.
Mandates that futures commission merchants and registered digital commodity entities hold customer digital assets with qualified digital asset custodians.

Protects software developers, node operators, and decentralized finance protocol participants from being regulated as intermediaries under the Act solely for performing basic blockchain network functions.
Establishes an Office of the Digital Commodity Retail Advocate within the CFTC to assist retail participants and propose regulatory improvements.
Authorizes the CFTC to collect registration and annual oversight fees from regulated digital commodity entities to cover implementation costs, and authorizes $150 million in appropriations.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for minimum capital requirements for digital commodity brokers and dealers, which are left to future CFTC rulemakings.
Specific fee rate schedules that the CFTC will establish for registrants.
The exact timeline for passage or enactment, as the bill has only been reported and placed on the Senate calendar.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act establishes a regulatory framework for digital commodities under the jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). It sets up registration, operational, and reporting requirements for digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers, and creates protections for software developers and customer asset segregation.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a comprehensive federal regulatory framework for the spot digital commodity market, assigning direct oversight authority to the CFTC while creating tailored definitions and protections for decentralized technology participants and customer assets.
